sources.title: Divine Revelation

sources.title: Degelman & Lynn (1995): Belief in Divine Intervention Scale

sources.title: Miracles
sources.claim: Miracle claims require conceptual separation from mere scientific unexplainedness and from generic belief in divine intervention.

sources.title: Divine Providence
sources.claim: Traditional theism includes divine agency and governance, but personal deity, providence, and miracle beliefs remain separable.

sources.title: Singelis (1994): The Measurement of Independent and Interdependent Self-Construals
sources.claim: Independent and interdependent self-construals can coexist; our relational-self items are not a validated administration of the Self-Construal Scale.

sources.title: Toleration
sources.claim: Toleration concerns conditional acceptance/noninterference with disapproved beliefs or practices and has multiple conceptions.

sources.title: Bastian & Haslam (2006): Psychological Essentialism and Stereotype Endorsement
sources.claim: Psychological essentialism includes biological basis, discreteness, and informativeness; our items only cover a subset.

sources.title: General and Personal Belief in a Just World scales
sources.claim: General belief in a just world concerns whether people broadly get what they deserve; it is distinct from personal just-world belief.

sources.title: Dunlap et al. (2000): Revised New Ecological Paradigm Scale
sources.claim: The revised NEP measures multiple facets of ecological worldview; our custom humanity-nature items are not the NEP scale.

sources.title: Murphy, Ackermann & Handgraaf (2011): Measuring Social Value Orientation
sources.claim: SVO measures social preferences in interdependent allocation choices; generic cooperation/competition beliefs are not equivalent to SVO.

sources.title: Federalism
sources.claim: Federalism divides authority between levels, while decentralization is broader; preference for local variation is not automatically federalism.

sources.title: The Ethics and Rationality of Voting
sources.claim: Epistocracy allocates political power partly by knowledge/competence; expert advice and expert rule are distinct.

sources.title: Revolution
sources.claim: Revolution, resistance, rebellion, secession, and reform are distinct; a preference for institutional rupture is not automatically endorsement of violent revolution.

sources.title: Iyer et al. (2012): Understanding Libertarian Morality
sources.claim: Liberty/oppression was developed as a proposed moral-foundation construct in work on libertarian moral psychology; it is not one of the six foundations validated in MFQ-2.

sources.title: Free Will (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
sources.claim: The existence, analysis, and moral significance of free will are distinct; causal explanation alone does not decide belief in free will.

sources.title: The Meaning of Life (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
sources.claim: Nihilism about meaning is distinct from rejection of cosmic purpose and from denial of a particular source of objective value.

sources.title: Political Legitimacy (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
sources.claim: Normative legitimacy concerns justified political power or authority; conditional authority differs from authority merely by office.

sources.title: Retributive Justice (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)

sources.title: Toleration (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
